messages:
maria_cs: quick weekly tailwatch for Acrolinx onboarding (week ending Jun 1) — focusing on p95/p99 by route + model and streaming vs non-streaming. TL;DR: streaming routes look fine at p95 but p99 is elevated on a couple routes, and spend nudged up ~7% w/w. please skim numbers + call out actions.

kevin_sre: raw numbers pulled from infra metrics (5m window rolling):
- /chat_stream (model=rwx-13b): p95=210ms p99=480ms
- /chat_sync   (model=rwx-13b): p95=190ms p99=360ms
- /embed-and-query (model=emb-2): p95=85ms p99=300ms
errors: stream routes 0.8% (mostly 5xx timeouts), sync routes 0.2%.
spend: customer spend +7% week-over-week, mostly on stream long-lived sessions.

ajay_eng: sounds like KV cache churn + smaller batch sizes for streaming. two quick guesses: long tail from frequent short sessions that don't warm cache, and partial-token streaming increases kernel switches. digging into session distribution now. snippet I used to slice sessions:```sql
SELECT session_id, count(*) as seq_len, avg(token_count) as avg_tokens
FROM request_logs
WHERE customer_id = 'acrolinx' AND ts >= NOW() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY session_id
ORDER BY seq_len DESC
LIMIT 50;```

sophie_csm: thanks — I'll prep enablement items for their CS team. action items for pre-call: ask for typical session length, whether they intentionally stream partial responses, and any recent prompt changes. i'll schedule a 30m sync for Mon 10am PT.

maria_cs: proposed short-term mitigations:
1) canary fallback: route-level fallback from chat_stream -> chat_sync for p99-sensitive traffic (10% canary).
2) suggest length-based batching: buffer very short sessions for 200ms to coalesce tokens (drop-in config change).
3) KV cache tune: extend session affinity TTL for Acrolinx to reduce cold misses.
renewal signal: MEDIUM risk — usage rising (good) but UX risk due to p99 spikes; recommend enablement + canary before renewal conversation.

kevin_sre: will open a rollout with canary + automatic rollback if p99 increases >10% vs baseline. opening runbook PR now. I set canary start at 10:30 PT and will watch these dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/acrolinx/tailwatch (private link).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for customer=acrolinx, route=chat_stream -> chat_sync fallback, traffic=10% (deployment id: canary-20240601-17).

ajay_eng: quick note — if we enable 200ms buffer, we should watch latency for short tail p95 to ensure we don't regress perceived responsiveness. will add experiment flag.

maria_cs: thanks team. next steps: @kevin_sre monitor canary for 2h and post p95/p99 diffs in this thread; @sophie_csm hold pre-call checklist and collect session examples from Acrolinx before Mon. i'll draft a short renewal note after we see canary outcome. :thumbsup:
